text:
Miriam: ACME support ticket — customers seeing 504s from hosted /v1/generate around 23:10 UTC. Spike ~150 reqs, mostly long prompts (>2048 tokens). Noted repeated hits to same runtime worker.
Jun: I saw the alert and started pulling traces. Initial hunch: kv-cache cold misses + batching + long seqlen pushing inference over client timeout.
ops-bot: alert: hosted-api-504-spike — region=us-east-1 — window=23:09:50..23:12:30 — failed=147, p95_latency=2400ms.
Miriam: Can you paste one of the failing request examples? ACME included a curl. request_id=r-8f3b9a2c
Jun: Trace snippet for r-8f3b9a2c: `queue_wait=1400ms -> model_infer=4100ms -> gateway_timeout=5000ms` — inference dominates.
Emily: Gateway client timeout is 5s for that route. With seqlen ~3k we see model_infer >4s on that worker. Repro locally with seqlen=3000 reproduces 504 within 25s when batching happens.
Raj: Can we reroute long-seq requests to dedicated small-batch pool? We have a `dedicated-longseq-us-east` pool but it's not in the routing rules. Could be a quick mitigation.
Tomas: Implemented temporary routing rule: seqlen>2048 -> dedicated-longseq-us-east, and bumped gateway timeout for ACME tenant to 30s. Change deployed 23:25 UTC. :white_check_mark:
Miriam: Support reports ACME errors dropped significantly after 23:30. Good catch. Emily, can you collect perf numbers and estimated cost delta for the dedicated pool?
Emily: Early numbers: p95 latency for ACME down from ~11s to ~2.2s after routing. CPU per-token up ~12% on dedicated pool vs shared, estimated hourly cost +18% for their traffic profile. Will run full bench and publish in the postmortem.
Jun: Proposed action items: 1) Create permanent routing rule for seqlen>2048 with sane default pool selection. 2) Add autoscaler pre-warm for KV cache when a tenant bursts large prompts. 3) Add a client-facing note about long prompts + recommend streaming/shorter prompts. 4) Add monitoring alert to detect worker queue depth spikes earlier.
Miriam: Assign owners: Jun (#1), Raj (#2), Emily (#3), Tomas (#4). I'll own customer comms and ticket closure. I'll open postmortem ticket PM-1402 and link logs/traces.
Support: ACME responded: "Thanks — overall improvement, we still see occasional micro-spikes during large bursts." They asked for a timeline for the permanent change.
Miriam: ETA for permanent routing rule by end of day tomorrow. We'll follow up with ACME and include mitigation guidance for burst pacing.
Jun: I'll drop the repro script and a few trace samples into PM-1402. Quick repro: `python repro_longseq.py --seqlen 3000 --concurrency 6 --model redwood-3b` replicates queueing scenario.
Tomas: Also note: one runtime worker (runtime-worker-42) showed a memory growth pattern during the window — adding to follow-up for eng-runtime.
Miriam: Thanks team. We'll capture root cause and action items in the postmortem. Closing thread once PM-1402 is triaged and ACME comms sent. :thumbsup:
